title: Committee of Supply – Head N (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head N (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

sections.label: China second largest economy
sections.summary: China has become the world's second largest economy, overtaking Japan in 2011.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: China has steadily moved up the ladder in economic size and has since become the world's second largest economy, overtaking Japan in 2011.

sections.label: US-China trade war
sections.summary: A trade war is developing between the US and China, and Singapore has been caught in the middle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: China has retaliated, and it appears a trade war is developing between these two economic giants, the two largest economies in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore, too, has been caught in the middle, with some of the US' tariffs affecting Singapore's goods unintentionally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: While reports from recent negotiations between both sides have appeared positive, prolonged tensions could have a severe impact on the global and regional economies.

sections.label: Group population and GDP
sections.summary: As a group, the countries account for over 600 million people and GDP of more than US$2.8 trillion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: As individual countries, we are relatively small, but as a group, we account for a population of more than 600 million with a gross domestic product (GDP) of more than US$2.8 trillion.

sections.label: Malaysian vessels in waters
sections.summary: Two Malaysian vessels came into Singapore's waters after new port limits were declared for Johor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: The most worrying recent developments have been the two Malaysian vessels that came into our waters following a declaration of new port limits for Johor.

sections.label: Suspension of restricted area
sections.summary: Mutual suspension of Malaysia's Restricted Area over Pasir Gudang and Singapore's Instrument Landing System procedures is effective until 31 March.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, the mutual suspension of Malaysia’s Restricted Area over Pasir Gudang and Singapore’s Instrument Landing System procedures will be effective until 31 March this year.

sections.label: Singapore Indonesia investment treaty
sections.summary: Singapore is Indonesia's largest investor, and a bilateral investment treaty and currency swap were discussed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Singapore is Indonesia’s largest investor, and I understand, at this retreat a bilateral investment treaty was discussed and a currency swap was also announced between the two countries.

sections.label: Singapore Cooperation Programme established
sections.summary: The Singapore Cooperation Programme was established in 1992 to train foreign government officials from developing countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In 1992, the Singapore Cooperation Programme (SCP) was established as the main platform for Singapore to give back to the international community through training programmes for foreign government officials from fellow developing countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last year, the World Bank ranked Singapore as the best country for developing human capital.

sections.label: Singaporeans travel overseas frequently
sections.summary: Singaporeans make more than 20 million overseas trips yearly, including overland journeys to Malaysia and beyond.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Singaporeans are among the most well-travelled in the world.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: They make more than 20 million trips overseas every year, including overland journeys to Malaysia, and venture beyond.

sections.label: Public expectations of assistance service
sections.summary: Public expectations of the quality and speed of assistance service have increased, and MFA has over 50 overseas missions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: At the same time, public expectations of the quality and speed of assistance service have increased.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I understand that MFA has over 50 overseas missions worldwide.

sections.label: US-China diplomatic relations anniversary
sections.summary: 1 March marks the 40th year of upgraded US-PRC diplomatic relations, when the US liaison office in Beijing became an embassy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: In fact, today, 1 March, marks the 40th year of the upgrading of diplomatic relations between the US and the PRC when the US liaison office in Beijing was converted to an embassy.

sections.label: US-China tensions and trade
sections.summary: US-China trade and investment grew to US$710 billion in 2017, but tensions increased in trade, Taiwan and the South China Sea.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: Whereas in the past, the US-China relationship was sometimes described as symbiotic with bilateral trade and investment between the two countries having grown exponentially reaching US$710 billion in 2017, the last two years have seen an increase in tensions between the countries, particularly on trade but also in other areas, including Taiwan and the South China Sea.

sections.label: US-Singapore trade and investment
sections.summary: Bilateral trade was nearly US$75 billion in 2017, with the US the largest foreign investor in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: Bilateral trade in goods and services was nearly US$75 billion in 2017 and, in that same year, the US continued to be the largest foreign investor in Singapore, while Singapore was the US' second largest Asian investor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: While on trade, a comprehensive and progressive agreement for the Trans-Pacific Partnership came into force at the end of last year, with the conspicuous absence of the US, which withdrew from its predecessor.

sections.label: Central and Eastern Europe growth
sections.summary: Central and Eastern Europe grow faster than the EU average, with nine of 12 high-growth EU members from the region.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Central and Eastern Europe are a rapidly growing region, with GDP growth significantly higher than the average in the European Union (EU).

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Last year, of the 12 EU members forecast to grow by 3% or more, nine were Central and Eastern European countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Romania’s GDP growth, for instance, hit 6.9% in 2017, though this figure fell to an estimated 4% last year, which is nonetheless significant.

sections.label: Singapore diplomatic and political exchanges
sections.summary: Singapore has a direct Warsaw flight, high-level exchanges with Russia, Turkey and Romania, and Czech plans to reopen its embassy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: There is now a direct flight from Singapore to Warsaw and, recently, we have had high-level political exchanges with Russia, Turkey and Romania.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I also note that Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis announced his intention to reopen the Czech Embassy in Singapore during his visit in January.

sections.label: ASEAN economic integration and GDP
sections.summary: ASEAN integration raised GDP per capita 70% from 2007 to 2017, with combined GDP of $2.77 trillion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Through the ASEAN Economic Community and other initiatives aimed at economic integration, GDP per capita increased by 70% from 2007 to 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The combined GDP of $2.77 trillion places ASEAN among the top 10 economies in the world.

sections.label: Singapore's ranking in last report
sections.summary: In the last report, Singapore came in 21st.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the last report, Singapore came in 21st.

sections.label: Singapore-China cooperation deals
sections.summary: Last September Singapore signed deals with China on Tianjin Eco-City replication, an NUS Chongqing institute, and Suzhou startups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, last September, we inked deals with China to promote the replication of the Tianjin Eco-City development in other Chinese cities, establish a National University of Singapore institute in Chongqing to conduct scientific research as well as technology transfer and commercialisation, and develop startups and partnerships in emerging industries in Suzhou.

sections.label: Soft power and smart nation
sections.summary: The Trump-Kim summit could have enhanced Singapore's soft power, and the ASEAN Smart Cities Network launch is welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, we could have made use of the Trump-Kim Singapore Summit last year to enhance our soft power when people all over the world were searching "where is Singapore".

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I also welcome the launching of the ASEAN Smart Cities Network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singapore should become a smart nation exercising smart power.

sections.label: US trade partner ranking
sections.summary: In 2017, the US was Singapore's third largest goods trading partner and top services trading partner.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In 2017 alone, the US was Singapore's third largest trading partner in goods and also its top trading partner in services.

sections.label: China-Singapore agreements signed
sections.summary: Singapore signed the China-Singapore FTA Upgrade Protocol and MOUs on Chongqing and Guangzhou cooperation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Notably, we signed the China-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (FTA) Upgrade Protocol, MOUs on Chongqing Connectivity Initiative – New International Land Sea Trade Corridor and the elevation of the China-Singapore Guangzhou Knowledge City to a state-level bilateral cooperation project.

sections.label: First US-DPRK Summit hosted
sections.summary: Singapore hosted the first US-Democratic People's Republic of Korea Summit in June 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Singapore hosted the first US-Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) Summit in June 2018.

sections.label: Second US-DPRK Summit outcome
sections.summary: The second US-DPRK Summit in Vietnam ended without a deal despite stated optimism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In fact, the US and DPRK held their second Summit in Vietnam over the past two days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, despite the stated optimism for both sides to achieve an agreement, no deal was concluded when the summit ended yesterday.

sections.label: Trade critical to Singapore
sections.summary: As a free and open economy, Singapore welcomes new trading partners and investment opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, as a free and open economy, trade is critical to Singapore and we welcome new trading partners and investment opportunities.

sections.label: Update on Africa Latin America Middle East
sections.summary: The question asks MFA for an update on engagement with Africa, Latin America and the Middle East.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: Would MFA provide an update on our engagement with these economies, specifically Africa, Latin America and the Middle East?

sections.label: Singapore ties with partner nation
sections.summary: The Currency Interchangeability Agreement since 1967 and defence cooperation underpin robust ties, and the question asks what steps Singapore is taking to strengthen the relationship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The Currency Interchangeability Agreement which has been embraced since 1967 and our strong defence cooperation also underpin the robust ties between our two nations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: What then are the steps that the Singapore Government is taking to continue strengthening the special relationship?

sections.label: Local arts groups international performances
sections.summary: Local arts groups including Theatre Practice, Siong Leng Musical Association, SCO, Singapore Symphony Orchestra and Singapore Dance Theatre have been invited or sent to perform at international arts festivals many times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Local arts groups, such as Theatre Practice, the Siong Leng Musical Association, the Singapore Chinese Orchestra (SCO), Singapore Symphony Orchestra, Singapore Dance Theatre, have all been invited or sent to perform at renowned international arts festivals on many occasions.

sections.label: Singapore arts groups overseas performances
sections.summary: Sri Warisan Som Said Performing Arts will perform at National Day celebrations in Melbourne, Theatre Practice brings Liao Zhai Rocks! to Shanghai, Ding Yi Music Company goes to the China ASEAN Music Festival, and SCO tours Europe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Sri Warisan Som Said Performing Arts, founded by Cultural Medallion recipient Mdm Som Said, will be performing at our National Day celebrations in Melbourne; the Theatre Practice is going to bring Liao Zhai Rocks! to the Shanghai Culture Square this March as part of their music season; Ding Yi Music Company is going to the China ASEAN Music Festival in May, too!

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The SCO is also heading to Europe on our international tour this year.

sections.label: European Strategic Cluster Partnerships initiative
sections.summary: The Commission introduced an initiative known as European Strategic Cluster Partnerships or ESCP-4i in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Commission introduced an initiative known as European Strategic Cluster Partnerships or ESCP-4i in 2016.

sections.label: EU ASEAN trade relationship
sections.summary: The EU is ASEAN's second largest trading partner, and in 2017 ASEAN exported almost €135 billion worth of goods and services into the EU.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The EU is ASEAN’s second largest trading partner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In 2017, ASEAN exported almost €135 billion worth of goods and services into EU.

sections.label: EU funding to ASEAN
sections.summary: The EU is the biggest donor to the ASEAN secretariat with €200 million for regional integration, plus €2 billion of bilateral support to ASEAN member states.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: EU is also the biggest donor to the ASEAN secretariat with funds of €200 million in support of ASEAN regional integration in addition to €2 billion of bilateral support to ASEAN member states.

sections.label: UNHCR Rohingya funding needs
sections.summary: The UNHCR needs $307.6 million in 2019 for Rohingya refugees and host communities' basic needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: At the same time, I know that the UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) needs $307.6 million in 2019 to meet the basic needs of the Rohingya refugees and the communities hosting them.

sections.label: Singapore-India bilateral trade 2017
sections.summary: In 2017 Singapore-India bilateral trade was S$25.2 billion, with each being the other's largest partner in their regions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In 2017, bilateral trade between Singapore and India was S$25.2 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Singapore was India's second largest trading partner in ASEAN while India was Singapore's largest trading partner in South Asia.

sections.label: Singapore Middle East investments 2012
sections.summary: Singapore's investments in the Middle East grew to more than $60 billion in 2012.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Singapore’s investments in the Middle East have grown to more than $60 billion in 2012.

sections.label: Question on investment growth
sections.summary: The passage asks how much investments have grown since 2012 and whether they have borne fruit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: How much have our investments grown since 2012 and have they borne fruit?

sections.label: EU-Singapore trade agreements approved
sections.summary: The European Parliament approved the EU-Singapore FTA and Investment Protection Agreement, with 84% of exports entering duty-free.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Chairman, the EU is our largest foreign investor and one of the largest global trading partners.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: So, it is good news that the strong EU-Singapore relations reached another milestone recently when the European Parliament approved the EU-Singapore FTA (EUSFTA) and the EU-Singapore Investment Protection Agreement.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: It is good news that 84% of our exports will be able to enter the EU duty-free, while the tariffs for the remaining products will be removed from the third to fifth year onwards.

sections.label: Canada-ASEAN trade 2017
sections.summary: Canada has stepped up regional engagement, with two-way trade with ASEAN member states rising to S$23.8 billion in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: However, in the recent years, it is evident that Canada has stepped up its engagement in the region.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: This is reflected in the two-way trade between Canada and the ASEAN member states, which increased to S$23.8 billion in 2017.

sections.label: CPTPP ratification by six signatories
sections.summary: Both countries were among the first six signatories to ratify the CPTPP in 2018, letting the agreement enter into force.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Both countries are also amongst the first six signatories that ratified the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) in 2018, allowing the agreement to enter into force.

sections.label: Arctic warming rate
sections.summary: The Arctic has been warming at twice the rate of any other place in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Arctic has been warming at twice the rate as any other place in the world.

sections.label: Trade and Singapore's GDP
sections.summary: Trade is about three times Singapore's GDP and has allowed it to thrive as an open economy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Trade is about three times our GDP and has allowed us to thrive as an open economy.

sections.label: CPTPP signing and entry into force
sections.summary: Singapore and 11 other countries signed a TPP version without the US, and the CPTPP came into force on 30 December 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On 8 March 2018, Singapore, together with 11 other countries, signed a version of TPP that did not include the involvement of the US.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: CPTPP was signed by Singapore and 11 other countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I understand that CPTPP has come into force on 30 December 2018.

sections.label: US share of global GDP
sections.summary: The US share of global GDP fell from 40% in 1960 to 24%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In 1960, American share of global GDP was 40%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: At that level, it was worth its while for the US to be a unilateral benefactor, umpire – global policeman, indeed – for the world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: But its share has now declined to 24% of global GDP.

sections.label: Shift to strategic rivalry
sections.summary: The dynamic between the two powers is shifting from engagement to strategic rivalry and competition.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: It will not allow the US or any other power to stop it from taking what it believes is its rightful place in the world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: This dynamic between the two powers is, therefore, shifting from one of engagement to one of strategic rivalry and competition.

sections.label: WTO trading system under threat
sections.summary: The global multilateral rules-based trading system embodied by the WTO is now under serious threat.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Fourth, the global multilateral rules-based trading system embodied by WTO is now under serious threat.

sections.label: CPTPP and RCEP progress
sections.summary: CPTPP was signed and came into force on 30 December 2018, and RCEP leaders committed to conclude negotiations later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Fortunately, with Japanese leadership and active support from the other 11 countries, we got the CPTPP signed, and then, to my pleasant surprise, enough of us ratified it so that it came into force on 30 December 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: CPTPP represents a market of approximately 500 million people and 22% of global trade and will provide our companies with increased market access in the Asia Pacific and these figures exclude the US.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: I am also happy to note that there has been substantial progress on the negotiations for the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), and leaders of all the RCEP participating countries have committed to conclude RCEP later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: If we get this done, it will encompass 45% of the world's population and amount to 30% of global GDP.

sections.label: US regional commitment initiatives
sections.summary: The US rolled out initiatives including US$113 million in new economic initiatives and US$300 million for regional security cooperation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The US has rolled out several initiatives to demonstrate its continued commitment to the region, including the US$113 million in new economic initiatives, and another US$300 million in funding for regional security cooperation.

sections.label: Singapore-China economic cooperation
sections.summary: Singapore remains China's top foreign investor, and both sides concluded the upgrade of the China-Singapore FTA in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: On the economic front, Singapore remains surprisingly as China's top foreign investor.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: While China has been our largest trading partner since 2013, both sides concluded the upgrade of the China-Singapore FTA in 2018, and this will bring our economic cooperation to new heights.

sections.label: ASEAN-China relations milestones
sections.summary: During Singapore's 2015-2018 coordination, the ASEAN-China FTA was upgraded toward goals of US$1 trillion trade and US$500 billion investment by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We also achieved several key milestones for ASEAN-China relations during the three years that we were the coordinator for that relationship from 2015 to 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We upgraded the ASEAN-China FTA, a big step towards our goal of achieving two-way trade in excess of US$1 trillion and investments of US$500 billion between ASEAN and China by 2020.

sections.label: Singapore hosted US-DPRK Summit
sections.summary: Singapore was asked to host the 1st US-DPRK Summit last June.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Singapore was asked to host the 1st US-DPRK Summit last June.

sections.label: Malaysia bilateral issues commitment
sections.summary: Singapore remains committed to resolving bilateral issues with Malaysia amicably, constructively, under bilateral agreements and international law.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: For Malaysia, although several bilateral issues have come to the fore in recent months, in fact, in just the last three months, we remain committed to resolving these issues in an amicable and constructive manner and in strict accordance with bilateral agreements and international law.

sections.label: Singapore Indonesia investment ties
sections.summary: Singapore was Indonesia's top foreign investor in 2018 with US$9.2 billion realised investments, and a US$10 billion bilateral financial arrangement was signed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Singapore remains Indonesia’s top foreign investor in 2018, with US$9.2 billion worth of realised investments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The US$10 billion bilateral financial arrangement, which was announced at the 2018 Leaders’ Retreat and signed on 5 November 2018, reflects the confidence in the economic fundamentals of both countries.

sections.label: Indonesia 2019 elections
sections.summary: Indonesia is on track to hold legislative and presidential elections on 17 April 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Indonesia is on track to hold legislative and presidential elections on 17 April 2019.

sections.label: FTA upgrade Enhanced Partnership
sections.summary: Negotiations to upgrade the bilateral FTA concluded last November, and work is ongoing to upgrade relations to an Enhanced Partnership.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In fact, we have just concluded negotiations to upgrade our bilateral FTA last November, and we are working to upgrade our relations to an Enhanced Partnership later this year.

sections.label: MFA lowest budget no increase
sections.summary: MFA has the lowest budget among Ministries, has not asked for an increase this year, and seeks more domestic support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In fact, I would like to remind the House, if you look at all the Ministries' Budgets, MFA is the lowest and MFA has not asked for an increase this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: What we are asking for is more domestic support.

sections.label: Singapore nimble independence prosperity
sections.summary: Singapore must stay nimble, seize opportunities while maintaining balance, and with support secure its independence, well-being and prosperity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: But this does not mean that we are powerless.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We must stay nimble, we must continue to seize opportunities whilst maintaining our balance in the midst of a rapidly evolving world, and we can do this with your support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We will secure Singapore's continued independence, well-being and prosperity.

sections.label: Counterterrorism, US access, investment
sections.summary: Singapore shared counterterrorism efforts, seeks renewal of 1990 US military access agreement, and reports investment rose to S$339 billion in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Last month, I attended the Meeting of the Ministers of the Global Coalition to Defeat ISIS in Washington DC to share Singapore's ongoing efforts to build regional counterterrorism capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We are working towards the renewal in 2020 of our 1990 landmark agreement granting the US access to military facilities in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Its investment has increased by some 21% from S$280 billion in 2016, to S$339 billion in 2017.

sections.label: ASEAN smart city pilot cities
sections.summary: The ASCN's 26 pilot cities set out ASEAN's smart city definition and city-specific action plans to become smart cities by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The ASCN's 26 pilot cities came together last year to set out ASEAN's definition of a smart city and develop city-specific action plans towards becoming smart cities by 2025.

sections.label: ASEAN-EU relations upgrade
sections.summary: ASEAN and EU Foreign Ministers agreed in principle to upgrade relations to a strategic level and reaffirmed multilateralism and a rules-based world order.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: At a recent meeting co-chaired by Minister Vivian Balakrishnan, the ASEAN and EU Foreign Ministers agreed in principle to upgrade ASEAN-EU relations to a strategic level and reaffirmed our shared commitment to multilateralism and a rules-based world order.

sections.label: Rakhine State needs assessment team
sections.summary: At Myanmar's invitation at the 33rd ASEAN Summit, Leaders agreed to despatch a needs assessment team to Rakhine State for the repatriation process.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: At Myanmar's invitation at the 33rd ASEAN Summit in November 2018, the Leaders agreed to despatch a needs assessment team to the Rakhine State to identify ways to support Myanmar's efforts in the repatriation process.

sections.label: No ASEAN human rights court
sections.summary: There are currently no ASEAN discussions on measures such as a Human Rights Court or a regional refugee and asylum policy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Currently, there are no discussions amongst ASEAN on pursuing measures, such as a Human Rights Court or a regional refugee and asylum policy.

sections.label: Malaysia extended Johor Bahru port limits
sections.summary: Malaysia unilaterally extended the Johor Bahru Port Limits on 25 October 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: On the port limits issue, as Members of the House are aware, Malaysia unilaterally extended the Johor Bahru Port Limits on 25 October 2018.

sections.label: ILS and RA suspension
sections.summary: After Foreign and Transport Ministers' meetings, both sides mutually suspended ILS procedures and permanent RA until 31 March this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Following the meetings between the Foreign Ministers on 8 January 2019 and the Transport Ministers on 23 January 2019, both sides have mutually suspended the ILS procedures and permanent RA until 31 March this year.

sections.label: Bilateral Financial Arrangement announcement

sections.label: ASEAN non-interference principle
sections.summary: The speaker says ASEAN's diversity means abandoning non-interference would fracture it, so moral suasion and quiet diplomacy are preferred.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Even the EU has its own challenges with differences among themselves.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But if you look at ASEAN, the 10 of us, size, economy, government systems, as I said before, ranging from monarchies, military arrangements, a variety of democracies, it would fracture ASEAN if we were to abandon that principle.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, I much rather our current practical approach, which is by moral suasion, by quiet diplomacy, discussion behind the scenes, and to tell our fellow members that, "yes, you have a problem within your borders, but it has impact on us.

sections.label: Non-interference and Malaysia water remarks
sections.summary: The speaker says non-interference cannot be abandoned, and cites Dr Mahathir's remarks urging Johor protests over the water deal.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: It predated ASEAN and we cannot force a quick resolution.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, that is why it is a long answer to the Member's question, but we cannot abandon the principle of non-interference.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: I think the Minister and Dr Mohamad Maliki both mentioned that efforts have been taken to make the relationship with Malaysia more constructive.

sentences.text: But just yesterday there were remarks by Dr Mahathir at a meeting with the Johor state government officials saying that he is encouraging people of Johor to protest against the current water deal to say it is unfair, and Singapore is a rich country, it should be more generous.

sentences.text: Any breach of the 1962 Water Agreement would call into question the Separation Agreement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Our obligation under the 1962 Water Agreement is to sell five million gallons per day, but actually, today, as we speak, we are selling around 16 million gallons per day.

sections.label: Singapore spending on Johor water
sections.summary: Singapore paid over S$300 million for the Linggiu Dam and has spent more than S$1 billion on water projects in Johor.

sentences.text: Johor owns the Linggiu Dam but Singapore paid more than S$300 million for its construction and operational costs, as well as compensation for the land used by the Linggiu Reservoir, and for the potential loss of revenue from logging activities, and also inclusive of a one-time payment of the lease of that land for the remaining tenure of the 1962 Water Agreement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Overall, we have spent more than S$1 billion on water projects in Johor, and this has helped not only PUB's water works but Johor's own water works, which are also extracting water from the same river.
